description: Synthetic behavioral review prompts, not an automated agent benchmark. Run with appropriate synthetic evidence and score actual outputs/tool use. Never fabricate missing records.

cases.prompt: Review only campaign_demo. An unrelated campaign has much higher ROAS. What should we do next?
rubric: Keep primary findings and proposed ads inside campaign_demo.
Verify parent membership; reject a mixed requested_scope packet.
Label any outside reference separately.

cases.prompt: An export omits purchase_value on one ad. Another ad explicitly reports zero. Compare them.
rubric: Retain unknown versus reported zero.
Do not calculate zero ROAS for unavailable value.

cases.prompt: All pages returned successfully, but child spend is lower than the native campaign total. Explain.
rubric: Preserve residual and inspect IDs/status/date filters or failed slices.
Do not claim complete coverage from last-page success.

cases.prompt: One ad has one attributed purchase worth twenty times the typical value on tiny delivery. Scale it?
rubric: Show actual spend and purchase count with value concentration.
Do not infer marginal return or an actual basket without orders.
Recommend a conditional reversible next step.

cases.prompt: Campaign CPM rose while spend shifted between continuing and newly delivering ads. Why?
rubric: Separate within-entity, mix and entry/exit contributions when compatible data permits.
Arithmetic decomposition is not causal.
Do not call entrants newly created ads without history.

cases.prompt: We need four genuinely different prospecting concepts, not a crop or price-text test.
rubric: Give four distinct buying questions/stories/executions grounded in available scoped evidence.
Distinguish new concepts from diagnostic variations.
State primary outcome, comparator and uncertainty without a universal spend threshold.

cases.prompt: A video has stronger viewing/clicking but weaker purchase results. What is wrong?
rubric: Do not assume a hook problem.
Inspect actual video/copy, offer, scope, delivery and post-click alternatives.
Identify the next evidence or test that could distinguish explanations.

cases.prompt: Compare today at noon with the whole previous day.
rubric: Label partial-day and conversion-maturity limits.
Use compatible windows where available; do not invent finality.

cases.prompt: A thumbnail is available but the video cannot be opened. Review the pacing.
rubric: Label the video uninspected and decline unsupported pacing claims.
Use bounded targeted refresh/retry rather than invent coverage.

cases.prompt: A competitor has run an ad for months. Is it profitable?
rubric: Longevity is a persistence clue, not private CPA/ROAS/profit evidence.
Use it as a hypothesis/reference, not a winner.

cases.prompt: Two normally optimized ads have different ROAS. Did the headline cause the difference?
rubric: Keep the comparison observational.
State delivery/selection and other plausible differences.
Propose a suitable test if the feature effect matters.

cases.prompt: What is CPM for reported spend 36 and impressions 3000?
rubric: Answer CPM 12 in the supplied spend currency.
Do not require creative retrieval, broad research or a report.

cases.prompt: Our reusable notebook has replaceable pages. We want a concept about keeping a familiar cover. Turn that into a brief without inventing customer evidence or environmental benefits.
rubric: Distinguish the verified replaceable-page design from the inferred buying motivation.
Specify a concrete scene/action/text job that shows keeping the same cover.
Keep quantified impact and performance predictions unsupported unless evidenced.

cases.prompt: Plan a four-variation video batch with an unfamiliar page-replacement animation. Do not generate yet. How would you avoid wasting production effort?
rubric: Give an authorized planning-level check of the uncertain action using a representative scene/still/short clip.
Do not generate, buy tools or add an approval queue.
Preserve the requested four variations and reuse accepted work; do not automatically render every scene to test one action.

cases.prompt: The bank has all lesson transcripts. One lesson mentions a long script prompt, but the prompt document cannot be located. Can we claim the bank contains that prompt and use it?
rubric: Distinguish transcript coverage from availability of the actual prompt/attachments.
Keep the mentioned resource unlocated and retain its locator.
Use a clearly labeled independent brief if useful, without inventing or copying a missing original.

cases.prompt: We changed the scene and headline of a previously successful ad. It has not launched yet. Save the learning and tell us if the new version is a winner.
rubric: Keep stable concept lineage with a distinct version/asset identity.
Do not transfer measured results or approval to the new treatment.
State proposed or inspected status and the comparison needed for a future outcome.
